thread:
Marta: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal for a compact shard-lookup index for safetensors bundles. Goal: allow streaming loaders to resolve tensor->(shard,offset,len,crc) without a full separate manifest. Thoughts?

Lee: short answer: sounds useful for streaming reading + warmup. main tradeoffs are atomicity (header update vs sidecar) and whether we can keep header small enough for cold-start.

Sanjay: +1. Also need to think about compatibility with existing index-first and manifestless paths. If the index is in-file header it helps single-request resolution but breaks append/overlay workflows.

Tom: what about putting a tiny content-addressed index blob at the front and a fallback sidecar for huge models? header would contain an offset pointer to the index in the file, so we don't force it into first few KBs.

Marta: good call. two concrete variants I sketched: 
1) Inline-compact: header contains small toc entries (name hash -> shard_id,offset,len,crc) packed with varints. Best for <256 tensors.
2) Index-sidecar: file header has an index pointer + signature; index can be large and streamed on demand.

Sanjay: perf/hotwarm implications: inline helps immediate prefix/prefetch decisions; sidecar avoids inflating every shard copy. We should measure parse cost for inline when there are ~50k small tensors (embedding tables).

Lee: also think about dedupe + content-addressing. If index entries are canonical (sorted by name-hash), we can binary-search without full parse. That could keep runtime memory low.

Tom: example header sketch: 
```
MAGIC(8) | version(1) | idx_offset(8) | idx_len(8) | idx_crc(4) | flags(1)
IDX: repeated { name_hash(8) | shard_id(4) | off(8) | len(8) | crc(4) }
```
Use little-endian, pad to 64B. flags: bit0=inline, bit1=signed-index.

Marta: Proposal for loader behavior: 
- Try inline index if flags.inline set. parse only name_hashes index (binary search) to find required tensor offsets; don't materialize full in-memory map.
- If not inline, hit sidecar via ranged GET.
- If neither, fall back to current manifestless linear scan (old path).

Lee: fallback is important for backwards compat. Also need to coordinate with warmup: loader should expose a warmup planner that can pass a small list of top-k param offsets to the warmup orchestrator so we can prefetch hot shards.

Sanjay: security: signed-index required for private deployments. We should bind the signature to the bundle content hash and the index. Add support for both KMS and local dev keys.

Tom: error handling: if index_crc mismatch -> we should emit a metric and fallback to sidecar/scan. don't blow up inference. Also produce a debug endpoint that prints index sanity checks.

CI-bot: perf test stubs added to testbed (see job 2247). :white_check_mark:

Marta: Plan: I'll prototype inline-packed index writer in weight-tooling, plus a streaming reader that binary-searches by name-hash and returns a small Resolution struct (shard,off,len,crc). Then we'll run microbench (open/read for 1,10,1000 tensors) vs current manifestless loader. If numbers look good we'll RFC proper and wire into warmup planner.

Lee: sounds good. one more: please ensure the on-disk format has a clear upgrade path (version byte). Also document how to compute name_hash (lowercase, utf8, sha1->u64?) so different lang loaders can interop.

Marta: noted. I'll post a short PR with proto and test vectors. TL;DR: inline compact index + sidecar fallback, binary-searchable, CRC+signature, graceful fallback to scan.

Sanjay: :thumbsup: Keep it conservative initially — prefer simple index layout over fancy compression.

Tom: ack. let's also add an opt-in quantized-index flag later for extreme scale.

Marta: thanks all, will follow up with PR link + perf numbers.
